public_rationale: Contemporaneous studies document real reliability problems, but those findings do not prove Marcus's universal negative. Other pre-post studies report classification accuracy around 97–99%, with some adaptation and consistency checks. These are substantial counterevidence. The retrieved records do not settle whether a candidate meets the stronger requirement of robust performance under representative operating variations. A categorical verdict would depend on an added reliability threshold.
limitations: High accuracy is evidence of useful capability and should not be dismissed merely because errors remain.
Benchmark success and dependable deployment are different evidentiary claims.
The candidate counterexamples are author-reported preprints.
Post-October-2024 model improvements were not used to judge the historical claim.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The anti-neurosymbolic tradition is limited. Its most visible manifestation, LLMs, has brought fame and money but no robust solution to solving any particular problem with great reliability.

statement.excerpt: But the anti-neurosymbolic tradition is limited; its most visible manifestation, LLMs, has brought fame and money, but no robust solution to solving any particular problem with great reliability.
statement.document_title: Two Nobel Prizes for AI, and Two Paths Forward

our_interpretation: Assess the substantive universal claim that LLMs had delivered no highly reliable solution to even one particular task.
The ordinary reading allows narrow practical tasks; it does not require general intelligence or perfect performance.
Robust reliability means consistently high task success on representative inputs, including ordinary variations, rather than one favorable example.
Prompting and fine-tuning are eligible. A separate symbolic solver doing the essential work would not directly test the claim about the anti-neurosymbolic tradition.
'Has brought' describes accumulated achievements through 9 October 2024. Later model capabilities cannot refute this historical observation.
'Fame and money' is background characterization, not a specified company financial metric.
criteria.support_condition: Broad evidence establishes that the claimed class had produced no qualifying reliable task solution by the post date. Failures on selected tasks alone are insufficient to establish this universal negative.
criteria.contradiction_condition: At least one LLM-based solution available by the post date demonstrates consistently high success on a defined practical task under representative conditions and ordinary variations.

evidence.explanation: The study finds persistent errors and sensitivity to natural variations in questions across the tested model families. This supports concern about reliability, but cannot establish that no particular reliable application existed.

CARP reports 97.39% accuracy on SST-2 and 98.78% on R8; its adaptation experiment retains 96.29% on SST-2 when demonstrations come from Yelp. These are material counterexamples to a weaker claim of no high-accuracy task performance, but do not fully establish operational robustness.

evidence.locator: Section VI-B; SMS results discussed in Section V-B
evidence.explanation: The study reports roughly 99% SMS-classification accuracy after fine-tuning and improved output consistency. This is a substantial candidate counterexample, but the retrieved evidence does not establish sustained reliability on representative deployment traffic and ordinary changes in that traffic.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A pre-post evaluation or deployment record establishing high, repeatable success on one defined practical task under representative variations, with an error tolerance appropriate to that task. Supporting the universal negative would require much broader coverage than the failure studies provide.
